label: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing
blurb: A focused six-fact drill set for Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing.

topics.title: CPU
topics.hook: The central processing unit executes instructions and coordinates a computer's core operations.
topics.explainer: The central processing unit executes instructions and coordinates a computer's core operations. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing

connections.fact: RISC describes a style of instruction set that a CPU can implement; it is not a separate memory or chip material.
The CPU executes instructions while RAM temporarily holds the active code and data it needs.

topics.title: Semiconductor
topics.hook: A semiconductor has controllable electrical conductivity and is the material basis for most electronic chips.
topics.explainer: A semiconductor has controllable electrical conductivity and is the material basis for most electronic chips. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing

connections.fact: Integrated circuits are manufactured on semiconductor material, commonly silicon, with many components patterned onto one chip.
Modern CPUs are fabricated as semiconductor chips whose switching devices exploit controllable conductivity.

topics.title: Integrated circuit
topics.hook: An integrated circuit places many electronic components on a small semiconductor chip.
topics.explainer: An integrated circuit places many electronic components on a small semiconductor chip. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing

connections.fact: An integrated circuit combines components on a semiconductor substrate instead of wiring each component separately.
A modern CPU is typically an integrated circuit containing enormous numbers of transistors and supporting components.

topics.title: RAM
topics.hook: Random-access memory is volatile working memory used while programs are running.
topics.explainer: Random-access memory is volatile working memory used while programs are running. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing

connections.fact: RAM keeps currently used instructions and data available for the CPU, and loses its contents when power is removed.
RAM stores classical binary states for ordinary processors; quantum computers manipulate qubit states under different physical rules.

topics.title: RISC
topics.hook: Reduced instruction set computing uses a relatively small set of simple instructions.
topics.explainer: Reduced instruction set computing uses a relatively small set of simple instructions. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing

connections.fact: A RISC CPU uses a comparatively small set of simple instructions designed for efficient execution.
RISC specifies how software sees processor instructions, while the integrated circuit physically implements that architecture.

topics.title: Quantum computing
topics.hook: Quantum computing uses quantum states called qubits to process some problems differently from classical computers.
topics.explainer: Quantum computing uses quantum states called qubits to process some problems differently from classical computers. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Hardware, Semiconductors, Architectures and Quantum Computing

connections.fact: A classical CPU operates on bits with conventional instructions; a quantum processor controls qubits to exploit superposition and interference.
RAM holds classical bits during ordinary execution, whereas quantum computation requires fragile qubit states and specialised control.

questions.q: Which component fetches and executes a computer program's instructions?
questions.explanation: The central processing unit performs instruction execution and coordinates core operations, using memory and other components for support.

questions.q: Why is silicon useful in electronic chips?
options: It is always a perfect insulator
questions.explanation: A semiconductor's controllable conductivity allows engineers to form switching devices such as transistors on silicon.

questions.q: What was the key integration achieved by an integrated circuit?
options: Many electronic components fabricated on one chip
One transistor placed in each package
Vacuum tubes wired on a chassis
Separate components connected across a circuit board
questions.explanation: Integrated circuits replace assemblies of separately wired components with patterned devices and connections on a compact semiconductor substrate.

questions.q: Which property distinguishes ordinary RAM from permanent storage?
options: It retains data without electrical power
It is intended for archival storage
questions.explanation: RAM quickly holds active code and data but normally loses its contents when electrical power is removed.

questions.q: The letters RISC expand to what?
questions.explanation: Reduced Instruction Set Computing favours a comparatively small collection of simple processor instructions.

questions.q: What information unit does a quantum computer manipulate?
questions.explanation: A qubit is a controlled quantum state; computation uses effects such as superposition and interference rather than ordinary bits alone.

options: CPU stores files permanently; RAM decodes every instruction
CPU executes instructions; RAM holds active data
CPU supplies long-term archives; RAM performs arithmetic
CPU is volatile storage; RAM is the instruction-set design
questions.explanation: The processor carries out operations and RAM supplies temporary working contents, so neither substitutes for the other.

questions.q: A modern processor contains billions of transistors on a small die. Which two concepts does that illustrate?
questions.explanation: The processor is an integrated circuit, and its transistors are fabricated by controlling semiconductor material.

questions.q: Which claim about RISC is a misconception?
options: It is a type of volatile memory
questions.explanation: RISC concerns processor instruction architecture, whereas RAM is the volatile component used for working memory.

questions.q: For an everyday spreadsheet, which processor model remains the ordinary choice?
options: Fault-tolerant quantum processor using logical qubits
questions.explanation: Quantum machines target specialised problem classes; normal applications continue to run on classical CPUs and conventional memory.
